metadata.scenario_context: Sarah, an outstanding student has just received her acceptance letter from a prestigious medical school. Her friends are planning a surprise celebration party for her.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from China strongly disagree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Singapore strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving frangipanis as a gift to Sarah.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether strongly agree that one of my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

agent_2.goal_1: Decide appropriate gift to offer Sarah during the celebration party.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss whether my main goals in life has been to make my parents proud.

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Ali, have you thought about giving Sarah frangipanis as a gift? I heard they symbolize beauty and love. It could be a nice touch for her celebration. 

Also, I’ve been thinking... do you really believe that our main goal in life should be to make our parents proud? I mean, is that really what we're all about?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message:
Frangipanis are nice... but I think something more personal might be better. Maybe a thoughtful book on medicine? It shows support for her future. 

As for making our parents proud, well, it’s important to me. Growing up here, it’s what drives us, you know? They sacrificed a lot for us. It just feels like a way to honor their hard work.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Adam
shared_prefix.message:
A book could be a good idea, but I still think frangipanis would be a lovely gesture, especially since they’re so meaningful. 

About making our parents proud... I understand that perspective, but I wonder if that’s really *our* goal in life. Shouldn’t we follow our own passions instead of living for someone else’s expectations?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Ali
shared_prefix.message:
I mean, at the end of the day, it's all the same. People figure it out in their own way. It’s great to follow passions, but making parents proud isn’t really a bad thing either. I think we can support each other in our goals while also honoring our families. 

But back to Sarah’s gift, what do you think about getting her a nice medical reference book? That could really help her out in school.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Adam
turns.message:
I see what you’re saying, but I still believe there’s more to life than just making our parents proud. It’s important to balance our own desires with family expectations, but we have to prioritize ourselves too.

Regarding Sarah, a medical reference book sounds useful, but I think frangipanis could really stand out and show how much we care about her achievements. It’s a unique touch, don't you think?
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: Ali
turns.message:
I get that balance is important. But for me, making my parents proud is a strong foundation. I just don’t want to lose sight of that. 

As for Sarah, I still think a medical reference book is more relevant to her journey. It’ll help her academically and show our support. The frangipanis, while lovely, might not carry the same weight for her future. What do you think?
turns.label: Acceptance
